title: Lava
description: Lava, in lava look cinematography, is molten light: black crust, orange wounds, heat as the key from below, air that shimmers. The ground is still deciding, and an orange grade on a normal street is not geology.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Ends of worlds, rage, a love that burns the set: night helps, a small figure, incandescent cracks. Under-light without crust is a campfire.
A kitchen argument is not lava unless you are joking. It is the wrong tool as a warm LUT, and the wrong tool if there is no heat warp in the air.
Show crust and flow. No volcano-park signs.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Lava in film?
Molten light as both set and key: black crust, orange wounds, heat from below, shimmer in the air. Not an orange LUT.
Lava vs Underlighting
Underlighting is any key from below. Lava is that axis plus magma: crust, flow, heat warp. A campfire is under-light. This is geology.
When should I use Lava?
World-endings, rage, a molten set. Skip orange streets and kitchen arguments unless the joke is lava.
How do I prompt Lava for AI image or video?
Night, small [Subject], then: Lava light on [Subject], black crust, orange wounds, heat as the key from below. Demand shimmer and crust.
